parsed.notes: Review confined to disclosed files only. I treated the lake's final treatment fields as controlling judgment evidence and did not raise support or quote-fidelity findings under Lens B.

reasons: Lake record is verified and non-stub, with identity fields matching United States v. Smith, Fifth Circuit, docket 23-60321, decided 2024-08-09.
Lake citations select 110 F.4th 817 as the official citation, and treatment remains good_law as of 2026-07-03.
residual_risks: No currency check beyond the disclosed as-of date.

reasons: Lens B does not attack taxonomy/support fit absent a treatment defect.
The underlying Smith authority is verified and the disclosed treatment record does not show it as dead law.
residual_risks: Substantive home-role support is outside Lens B.

reasons: As a case-holding assertion, the disclosed treatment record marks Smith good_law only on a varies-by-point composite basis.
The general-warrant component is separately cautioned and limited by Chatrie while still marked bound in the Fifth Circuit, so the current-treatment caveat is captured elsewhere on the page.
residual_risks: If this holding is reused without the treatment section, the general-warrant sentence could look broader than the current treatment permits.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Pair standalone uses of the holding with the Chatrie caution and Fifth Circuit limitation.

reasons: Lens B sees no disclosed currency defect in treating Smith as a Fifth Circuit geofence anchor.
The lake point override says the categorical geofence-general-warrant point is still bound in the Fifth Circuit, though cautioned after Chatrie.
residual_risks: Substantive home-role support is outside Lens B.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: If space permits, specify that the anchor role is Fifth Circuit/geofence and subject to the Chatrie caution.

reasons: The payload matches the lake treatment judgment: field_i_validity good_law, as_of_content/as_of_treatment 2026-07-03, composite_basis principal-holding, and composite_basis_ref search.digital.geofence-threshold.
The lake expressly accounts for Chatrie by marking treatment varies_by_point and by cautioning the categorical general-warrant point.
The controlling negative lane for SCOTUS/Fifth Circuit reports proposed_negative_events 0; the negative-looking progeny edges are proposed, unpointed, and marked only as mentioned.
residual_risks: Disclosed progeny includes proposed noncontrolling negative labels, but the lake's final treatment judgment does not treat them as overruling or abrogating Smith.
No external post-2026-07-03 currency review was performed.

reasons: The treatment override matches the lake: point search.warrant.geofence-general-warrant, field_i_validity caution, s3_binding_status bound, and Chatrie listed as limited.
The lake scope note states that the point remains binding in the Fifth Circuit while SCOTUS declined to adopt the categorical rule, which supports the caution label.
residual_risks: No separate Chatrie authority record is disclosed; this review relies on the Smith lake treatment judgment fields as permitted.

reasons: Lake identity identifies Smith as a U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit decision with circuit 5th.

The disclosed treatment record shows no controlling SCOTUS or Fifth Circuit negative event, and the point override says the cautioned geofence-general-warrant point remains bound in the Fifth Circuit.
residual_risks: The weight label should not be read as national binding authority.
